title: Checking whether an F4SE plugin (DLL) really loads: reading f4se.log
content:
Checking whether an F4SE plugin (DLL) really loads: reading f4se.log
F4SE writes Documents\My Games\Fallout4\F4SE\f4se.log every time the game starts through f4se_loader. It first lists every DLL it finds ("checking plugin X.dll") and only further down, after all of those, writes one result line per DLL:
- "plugin X.dll (00000001 Name 00000002) loaded correctly (handle 5)": the plugin runs.
- "plugin X.dll (00000000  00000000) no version data 0 (handle 0)": F4SE rejected it, usually because it was built for another game version (for example a 1.10.163 DLL on game 1.11.240). Nothing that mod's DLL does happens in game, even though the mod looks installed.
The result line can be 70 or more lines below the "checking" line, so look for the result line by name.
If a DLL is not in the log at all: it was installed after the last game start (start the game once and look again), or the game was not started through f4se_loader. The first line ("F4SE runtime: initialize (version = 0.7.9 010B0F00 ...)") shows the F4SE version and the game version it ran on (010B0F00 = 1.11.240).
tags: f4se.log plugin loaded correctly no version data dll not loading f4se plugin check which mods load runtime version
verified_by: A real f4se.log from F4SE 0.7.9 on game 1.11.240 (118 lines): 'checking plugin' lines at lines 13-30, result lines from line 86; f4ee.dll 'loaded correctly', DiverseBodiesRedux.dll 'no version data', 2026-11-06.

title: Realistic NPC mods on Fallout 4 1.11.240: what loads (LooksMenu, Diverse Bodies Redux, CBBE physics)
content:
Realistic NPC mods on Fallout 4 1.11.240: what loads (LooksMenu, Diverse Bodies Redux, CBBE physics)
Checked on a game at 1.11.240 with F4SE 0.7.9:
- LooksMenu 1.7.0.4 (f4ee.dll) loads.
- Diverse Bodies Redux's DiverseBodiesRedux.dll is rejected ("no version data"): its page requires game 1.10.163 (not next-gen) and exactly the official LooksMenu 1.6.20. Its female presets are for CBBE; its male presets are for the BodyTalk male body. Its random bodies, heads, overlays and skins never apply on 1.11.x, although its data files are installed. Its body presets (DiverseBodiesRedux\BodymorphsFemale and BodymorphsMale, slider name and value lists) can be turned into LooksMenu BodyGen templates, which do work on 1.11.x.
- CBBE OCBP Jiggle Mania is only an ocbp.ini settings file. It does nothing without a physics DLL. Its file has playerOnly=1 (physics on the player only, not NPCs) and femaleOnly=1.
- OCBP LPCE physics (Nexus 105699) has an AE build whose cbp.dll is for 1.11.191, 1.11.221 and 1.11.240. It is standalone: install only one physics DLL (two cause crashes). It reads ocbp.ini settings in the same format, but its solver differs from old OpenCBP 2.2.1, so old presets need retuning in its in-game editor. Its editor hotkey is F7 (cbp_config.ini Hotkey = 0x76), the same as Commonwealth Engine Fixes' shadow toggle (FCShadow2.ini iToggleKey 0x76): change one of them.
- CBBE's archives contain only textures and materials, no body mesh: the CBBE body exists only after BodySlide builds it.

title: LooksMenu BodyGen and face tint size: where the files go and what they need
content:
LooksMenu BodyGen and face tint size: where the files go and what they need
BodyGen (random body shapes per NPC) is part of LooksMenu. Its files are Data\F4SE\Plugins\F4EE\BodyGen\<plugin name>\templates.ini and morphs.ini (file names ending in _templates.ini / _morphs.ini are read too). It must be switched on in f4ee.ini, [BodyMorph] bEnable=1 and bEnableBodyGen=1. Syntax (no comment lines: LooksMenu logs lines without '=' as errors):
- templates.ini, one body per line: Name=Slider@value, Slider@min:max ... A comma means 'all of these'; min:max gives each NPC a random value in that range. Values are BodySlide values divided by 100 (50 in a BodySlide preset = 0.50). Example: Athletic1=Hips@0.45:0.75, MuscularArms@0.85:1, Belly@-0.3:-0.1
- morphs.ini, who gets which body: All|Female|HumanRace=Athletic1|Curvy2|Slim3 (a pipe means LooksMenu picks one per NPC). For one NPC: Fallout4.esm|2F1E=Athletic1 (plugin|FormID). Children use another race (HumanChildRace), so 'All|Female|HumanRace' never reaches them.
- Slider names must exist on the built body: LooksMenu's sliders.json for that body lists them (CBBE has 83). Male presets need a male body with sliders (e.g. BodyTalk).
When it works, LooksMenu's own log (f4ee.log) says "Generated N BodyMorphs for <actor>".
BodyGen and LooksMenu body sliders change the body through morph data, so the body mesh must be built in BodySlide with "Build Morphs" ticked (that writes a .tri file next to the body .nif, e.g. Meshes\Actors\Character\CharacterAssets\FemaleBody.tri). If the winning FemaleBody.nif has no .tri beside it, NPC bodies do not change.
Face tints: f4ee.ini [CharGen] uTintWidth / uTintHeight set the size LooksMenu paints face tints at (default 1024). LooksMenu's own comment says to make them the same as the face textures. VEFS warns that face, face detail and tint textures of different sizes cause "rusty" faces. With a 2K face texture (BaseFemaleHead_d.dds 2048x2048), set both to 2048.

title: Mod Organizer 2: which copy of a file wins, and mods installed one folder too deep
content:
Mod Organizer 2: which copy of a file wins, and mods installed one folder too deep
- Loose files always beat files inside BA2 archives.
- Among loose files, the mod lower in Mod Organizer's left pane (higher priority) wins. In the profile's modlist.txt the order is reversed: the first line is the highest priority ('+' enabled, '-' disabled, '*' DLC/Creation Club).
- Archives (.ba2) load with the plugin whose name they start with ("X-SensuousCore - Textures.ba2" with X-SensuousCore.esp), so the plugin must be active; between archives, the later plugin in the load order wins.
- A mod whose files sit in an extra folder (<mod>\Data\Meshes\... instead of <mod>\Meshes\...) is ignored by the game for those files, even when enabled. Reinstall it, or move the contents of that inner Data folder up one level.
- A quest or NPC mod can carry its own FemaleBody.nif inside its archive and silently replace the body you expect.

title: Fallout 4 tattoos: LooksMenu body overlays vs face tattoos, and why face-tattoo mods break LMCC
content:
Fallout 4 tattoos: LooksMenu body overlays vs face tattoos, and why face-tattoo mods break LMCC
There are two different kinds of tattoo mods:
- Body tattoo packs are LooksMenu overlays. Each pack has Data\F4SE\Plugins\F4EE\Overlays\<plugin>\overlays.json, a list of {"id", "name", "slots": [{"slot": 3, "material": "...BGEM"}], "playable", "gender"} (gender 1 = women, 0 = men), and its plugin must be active. In game they appear in LooksMenu's Body > Overlays. Examples: Tattoos Collection by Dreivor (283 designs, listed for both women and men, plus 60 full-body sets), Rutah Tattoo Pack (CBBE, 47), Alysraza Tattoos (CBBE and SHB, with separate _Male versions), DNX Body Tattoos (28). Nail polish, pubic hair and body hair packs use the same overlay system but are not tattoos.
- Face tattoos and face paints (LooksMenu Customization Compendium, RoboAsimov's Lore-Friendly Tattoo-a-palooza, warpaint, makeup) are tint entries on the human race record. Every mod that edits the human race record replaces the others' version, and the last one loaded wins. So a face-tattoo or face-paint mod loaded after LMCC removes LMCC's face options (or the other way round). Fix: load LMCC (or its patch) last, or make a merged patch in xEdit that keeps both tint lists. Body overlay packs do not touch the race record and never conflict with LMCC.
To see which mods edit the human race: in xEdit look at Fallout4.esm > Race > HumanRace (00013746) and check which plugins override it.

title: Putting LooksMenu tattoos (overlays) on NPCs from a Papyrus script
content:
Putting LooksMenu tattoos (overlays) on NPCs from a Papyrus script
LooksMenu ships its Papyrus API source in its archive (Scripts\Source\User\Overlays.psc and BodyGen.psc). Overlays:
- struct Entry { uid, priority, template, red, green, blue, alpha, offset_u, offset_v, scale_u, scale_v }
- Overlays.AddEntry(Actor akActor, bool isFemale, int priority, string template): adds one overlay by its id from an overlays.json.
- Overlays.Add / Remove / Set / Get / RemoveAll, Overlays.GetAll(Actor, bool isFemale) returns Entry[].
- Overlays.Update(Actor) applies the changes; call it once after adding.
BodyGen.psc also has SetMorph / GetMorph / RegenerateMorphs and SetSkinOverride(Actor, string id) for a per-NPC skin.
In your own script the struct type from another script is written with a colon: Overlays:Entry[] list = Overlays.GetAll(a, female). The '#' form (Overlays#Entry) does not compile in Fallout 4 ("no viable alternative at character '#'").
A simple NPC tattoo script: a start-game quest whose script uses Game.GetPlayer().FindAllReferencesWithKeyword(ActorTypeNPC (Fallout4.esm 00013794), radius) on a timer, skips a.IsChild(), the player, ActorBase.IsUnique() if wanted, and anyone whose GetAll(...) already has entries, remembers handled NPCs in a FormList (AddForm / HasForm), then calls AddEntry for a few templates and Update. Compile it against LooksMenu's Overlays.psc (add its folder to the compiler's import list).
